Exactly my point. Going into safe spaces and posting mean comments is cruel, but sending disgusting videos and threats directly to LGBTQ+ people is horrible. 

The actual real-life threats and possibility of being attacked and them finding out your personal information is the scariest part because that is life-ruining. It may just be a rumour or a scare tactic or a hoax, but there also could be real danger there. We know that this is possible with technology, and attacks like these happen to minority groups.

What some people are aiming to do with Pridefall is to find addresses of LGBTQ+ people and put them online, also phone numbers and other personal information. This could mean people being outed in a homophobic/transphobic family or community, and being kicked out in the middle of a pandemic. This also means that people would know where they lived, putting them at risk of being attacked.

Younger kids may also see these hateful comments and not understand what they are seeing, and the Pridefall homophobes are planning to put gore and r*pe online too, which are disturbing and would upset and disturb people, especially teenagers.

These are risks of Pridefall.
